scenes.heading: Delta Tables
scenes.narration: A Delta table stores your data as Parquet files governed by a transaction log, giving you reliable, versioned tables.

scenes.heading: Two kinds of Delta tables
bullets: Managed: Databricks owns the storage location
External: you point at your own path
Both share the same Delta reliability
scenes.narration: A managed table lets Databricks control where the data physically lives and cleans it up when you drop the table. An external table points at a path you own, so dropping the table leaves the files in place. Both flavors get the same ACID guarantees and time travel from Delta.

scenes.heading: Creating a Delta table
scenes.code:
df = spark.read.csv('/mnt/raw/new_customers.csv', header=True, inferSchema=True)

# Write as a managed Delta table
df.write.format('delta').mode('overwrite').saveAsTable('customers')

# Or write to a specific path (external)
df.write.format('delta').save('/mnt/delta/customers')
scenes.narration: Here we read a CSV into a DataFrame with an inferred schema. Calling saveAsTable creates a managed Delta table registered in the catalog. Alternatively, using save with an explicit path writes an external Delta table you control directly.

scenes.heading: What Delta creates on disk
scenes.narration: On disk, Delta writes your rows into Parquet data files. Alongside them it maintains a hidden delta log directory. Each transaction adds a JSON commit, and periodic checkpoints compact the log so reads stay fast.

scenes.text: Prefer managed tables in Unity Catalog for governance; use external tables only when another system must own the files.
scenes.narration: Prefer managed tables in Unity Catalog for easier governance, and reserve external tables for cases where another system must own the underlying files.
